frozen_decisions_applied: FD-16 (by extension, not literally named in earlier stages): the PersistedMatterEndpointState enum (kUnassigned/kAssigned/kPendingRemoval) S3 reserved is exactly the state machine this allocator implements, though via its own independent store -- see docs/architecture/MATTER_ENDPOINT_IDENTITY.md Section 2.2 for why.

FD-01 extended to Matter identity: a device rejoining mid-removal (kPendingRemoval) is never allowed to inherit its own not-yet-confirmed slot; it is treated exactly like a genuinely new device and gets a fresh allocation. No state is guessed or inherited across a rejoin.

S4 required change #20: MatterEndpointRegistry is keyed exclusively by core::DeviceId; one endpoint carries every cluster class (temperature/occupancy/contact) a device supports -- matter_bridge.cpp's sync_snapshot() no longer resolves a separate endpoint per cluster.
S4 required change #21: dynamic base 10, capacity service::kServiceMaxDevices (64, confirmed equal to core::kMaxDevices), reviewed range 10-73.

S4 required change #22/#25: the three fixed class-wide constants (kMatterEndpointTemperature/Occupancy/Contact = 10/11/12) and the entire MatterEndpointMapEntry/set_endpoint_map mechanism are deleted from the codebase, not merely deprecated -- nothing production-relevant consumed them once endpoint resolution moved server-side and DeviceId-keyed. Locked by INV-H008.

S4 required change #23: allocation happens in ServiceRuntime::sync_matter_endpoint_allocations(), called before the read-model snapshot matter_bridge consumes is rebuilt; a new allocation triggers persist_current_core_state() before that snapshot becomes visible (the CoreState-side persist; the Matter registry's own store is written synchronously inside allocate() itself).

S4 required change #24: two-phase removal (mark_pending_removal -> HAL tombstone attempt -> confirm_removed only on HAL success) is fully implemented and tested; the HAL tombstone primitive (hal_matter_remove_endpoint) is new in this pass, following the codebase's existing weak-hook pattern exactly.

S4 required change #26: a short-address remap (INV-ID-01 in core_reducer.cpp: same DeviceId, new short_addr, still online, no intervening leave) cannot disturb an existing Matter allocation by construction, since the registry's API has no short_addr parameter anywhere. Verified end-to-end, not just at the allocator's isolated API level.

S4 required change #27: hal_matter_available()'s existing truthful-unavailability contract (host=true for testability, ESP_PLATFORM weak-hook default=false) was already correct before this pass and is unchanged; hal_matter_remove_endpoint() follows the identical pattern.

matter_endpoint_registry.detail: DeviceId-keyed allocator with its own independent two-generation NVS store (mtep_a/mtep_b), replicating persisted_state_store.cpp's write/validate/commit protocol over a differently-shaped, much smaller payload rather than retrofitting that class to be generic. Deterministic lowest-free-slot allocation, idempotent re-allocation, explicit kNoCapacity at exhaustion, full two-phase removal, fail-safe (not fail-closed) recovery from a corrupted store. Tested in test_matter_endpoint_registry.cpp: 7 scenarios covering every one of the above plus persistence across a simulated reboot for both the assigned and pending-removal states.

removal_wiring.status: COMPLETE, TESTED (host); ESP_PLATFORM real-adapter path unverifiable
removal_wiring.detail: ServiceRuntime::handle_matter_endpoint_removal_on_device_left(), called from apply_managers() on kDeviceLeft, resolves the leaving DeviceId (falling back to the locator registry if the event itself lacks one, since the registry is still queryable at this point -- core_reduce, which wipes the CoreDeviceRecord, runs AFTER apply_managers in the event loop), then attempts the new hal_matter_remove_endpoint() HAL primitive and only confirms removal on success. New HAL primitive follows the exact existing weak-hook pattern (hal_matter_stack_remove_endpoint, ESP_PLATFORM default -1/unavailable, host stub returns 0/success). Tested end-to-end (host, where the tombstone succeeds) in test_matter_endpoint_remap_stability.cpp's second half.

allocation_wiring_and_remap_stability.detail: ServiceRuntime::sync_matter_endpoint_allocations(), called from notify_read_models_from_core_snapshot() before the Matter read-model snapshot is rebuilt, allocates for every online device with a resolved DeviceId (deliberately not gated on capability discovery -- see docs/architecture/MATTER_ENDPOINT_IDENTITY.md Section 2.4 for why) and persists the CoreState side if any new allocation happened. Because the registry's entire API is DeviceId-only, a short_addr remap cannot reach it at all, which is what makes item #26 hold by construction. Tested end-to-end in test_matter_endpoint_remap_stability.cpp: endpoint unchanged across a pure remap; a genuinely different physical device after a confirmed removal correctly lands on the freed slot without any short_addr-based coincidence being load-bearing.

matter_bridge_simplification.detail: MatterEndpointMapEntry/set_endpoint_map/kMatterEndpointTemperature/Occupancy/Contact and the matter_endpoint_map.hpp/matter_device_map.cpp file pair are deleted outright (confirmed by repository-wide grep: zero remaining references anywhere, including test/target). matter_bridge.cpp's sync_snapshot() now reads the single pre-resolved device.endpoint field for every attribute type instead of a per-cluster class lookup -- a direct simplification following from 'one endpoint per device' rather than a separate refactor. All 7 affected matter_bridge/matter_runtime host tests updated: three that constructed a MatterBridgeSnapshot directly now set .endpoint on the struct; three that exercised the real ServiceRuntime pipeline switched from raw CoreEvent posting to identity-aware HAL simulation (hal_zigbee_simulate_device_joined_with_identity), since MatterEndpointRegistry -- correctly -- refuses to allocate for a device with no resolved DeviceId.

bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_pass.detail: matter_endpoint_registry.cpp's occupied_count() used a raw counting loop; cppcheck's core+service job flagged it (useStlAlgorithm), converted to std::count_if with a lambda, re-verified cppcheck exit 0.

test_isolation_bug_found_and_fixed_in_ow.status: FIXED, CONFIRMED BY TEST FAILURE THEN PASS
test_isolation_bug_found_and_fixed_in_ow.detail: The host hal_nvs mock only clears its backing storage on the very first hal_nvs_init() call in a process (simulating first boot); every later call in the same test binary is a no-op. test_matter_endpoint_registry.cpp's first draft called hal_nvs_init() at the top of each of its 7 test functions expecting a fresh store each time, which is not what the mock does -- state accumulated across functions within the one process, causing test_capacity_exhaustion_is_explicit to fail (residual entries from earlier functions left fewer than 64 free slots). Fixed by adding a force_clean_matter_store() helper that overwrites both NVS blob keys with mismatched-length garbage (forcing MatterEndpointRegistry::load() to treat them as corrupt/absent, its documented fail-safe path) at the start of every test function, rather than relying on hal_nvs_init()'s misunderstood reset semantics.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Matter endpoint persistence uses its own independent NVS store rather than the S3 PersistedDeviceRecord.matter_endpoint_state/matter_endpoint_id fields that appear to have been reserved for exactly this purpose.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: A kPendingRemoval endpoint must remain non-reusable across the corresponding CoreDeviceRecord being wiped (core_reducer.cpp's kDeviceLeft handling does this immediately) and across reboot until tombstone confirmation. Once the device has left Core, there is no PersistedDeviceRecord slot left to carry that fact forward -- the S3 payload's per-device shape is fundamentally the wrong fit for state that must outlive the corresponding device record. See docs/architecture/MATTER_ENDPOINT_IDENTITY.md Section 2.2 for the full reasoning, including why PersistedStateStore itself was not made generic and reused (it is hardcoded to PersistedStatePayload and INV-H006 pins its existence/shape by name; retrofitting it risked destabilizing already-shipped, tested S3 code for a moderate, avoidable amount of duplication).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: S3's matter_endpoint_state/matter_endpoint_id fields remain unpopulated dead schema (round-trip only, never written or read) unless a future pass decouples Matter endpoint lifecycle from Core device lifecycle in that schema. No regression: those fields were never populated by anything before this pass either (S3-completion.json documented them as 'structural readiness only').

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Endpoint allocation is not gated on capability discovery (has_temperature/occupancy/contact known); every online, identity-resolved device gets an endpoint immediately on join.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: An earlier draft gated allocation on capability discovery, but this made allocation timing dependent on Zigbee interview completion order and broke test compatibility for the pre-existing bridge/runtime-feed test suite (which posts raw join events with no capability data). Re-examined the plan's own test list: nothing in it requires capability-gated allocation, only DeviceId-keyed allocation and deterministic lowest-free assignment, both of which hold either way. Simplified to unconditional allocation on join.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A device that joins but never reports any Matter-relevant attribute permanently occupies an endpoint slot with no active clusters until it leaves. Capacity is shared 1:1 with core::kMaxDevices (both 64), so this can never cause capacity exhaustion under normal operation; it is a minor efficiency note, not a correctness gap.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Plan item #22's BLOCKED_DELTA_REVIEW build-time gate (fail if any additional static/reserved target endpoint conflicts with the 10-73 range) is not implemented as a generic build check.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: A repository-wide search confirmed no other static/reserved Matter endpoint constant exists anywhere in the codebase today (the three that did are deleted by this pass). There is currently nothing for such a gate to find. INV-H008 locks the specific regression this repository could reintroduce (the deleted constants coming back); a generic diff-every-constant gate is deferred as its own reviewable increment rather than built speculatively.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: If a future change introduces a new hardcoded Matter endpoint constant outside MatterEndpointRegistry's [10,73] allocation path, INV-H008 would not automatically catch it unless it happens to match one of the three deleted names. Documented in docs/architecture/MATTER_ENDPOINT_IDENTITY.md Section 3.4 as an explicit, reviewed gap, not an oversight.
